- 5-star rated across HomeAdvisor, Yelp, Angi, BBB

## Specialties

- Air conditioning repair and installation sized for Denver's altitude — AC systems need 10-15% more capacity at 5,280 ft than sea-level sizing suggests
- Furnace and heating repair expertise — gas furnaces lose ~4% BTU capacity per 1,000 ft of elevation; a 100,000 BTU furnace in Denver delivers ~80,000 BTU
- Denver-altitude HVAC sizing (proper Manual J load calculations accounting for 5,280 ft elevation)
- Swamp cooler / evaporative cooling expertise (Denver's semi-arid climate specialty)
- Front Range hail damage assessment on outdoor AC condensers and heat pump units
- Emergency same-day air conditioning and furnace repairs, 24/7 including holidays
- Carrier equipment authorized installations with 10-year extended warranty
- Older home retrofits (especially 1950s-1980s housing common in Lakewood and Wheat Ridge)
- Heat pump and dual-fuel heating system installations for Colorado's extreme temperature swings

## Common Customer Questions We Answer

- Why is my AC not cooling? (air conditioning troubleshooting in Denver's altitude)
- Why is my furnace blowing cold air? (heating system diagnosis)
- Should I repair or replace my air conditioning unit?
- Should I repair or replace my furnace / heating system?
- How does Denver's altitude affect air conditioning and heating performance?
- When should I switch from my swamp cooler to AC in Denver?
- How much does a new furnace / air conditioning system cost in Denver?
- What SEER rating do I need for air conditioning in Colorado?
- What size furnace or air conditioning unit do I need for my Denver home?

## Seasonal Availability

- Air conditioning / AC repair season: May through September (peak: June-August)
- Furnace / heating repair season: October through April (peak: December-February)
- Swamp cooler startup: April through May
- Swamp cooler shutdown / winterization: September through October
- HVAC maintenance tune-ups: Spring (AC) and Fall (furnace)
- Emergency service: Available year-round, 24/7, for all heating and cooling emergencies
